title: Jurisdiction map: rules on amusement rides and rider-supplied equipment
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Whether parks may allow rider-supplied restraint equipment depends on jurisdiction: US states adopt ASTM F24 differently; the EU, UK, Canada, Japan and Australia have their own regimes.
objective: Map, per jurisdiction (all US states with ride programs, plus EU, UK, Canada provinces, Japan, Australia), the regulator, which ride standards are adopted, and any public rule on rider-supplied equipment or ride modifications.
acceptanceCriteria: Each row cites the statute, regulation or regulator page
Clear note that this is not legal advice
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
